title: How do you guys market your games developed using AI assistance?
author: yapdakilla81
selftext: Since majority of Reddit and Discord channels are blocking games with gen AI usage?

comments.author: Charming_You_25

replies.author: Weaves87
replies.body:
I have never used Reddit ads before but I've heard their conversion rate is abysmal. They're better if you're trying to build a brand, not sell a product.

You should focus on finding content creators that play the genre/kind of game that you are making. Head over to YT/Twitch and start building a list of creators that you think would vibe with the game. Research their content and come up with a pitch for why your game would be perfect for their stream/community/video/etc. Then send them an email and see if they are open. There are a lot of smaller content creators out there that will gladly check your game out (for free) just for the new content alone. You just need to get your game on their radar when they have a little downtime to explore something new.

Marketing an AI game is not different from marketing a non-AI game. If the game is fun, cohesive, and well designed, people will play it and will also probably pay for it at the right price. You just need to get it in front of the right people who will get the word-of-mouth ball rolling for you

comments.body: I have my hermes agent do a tweet twice a week on my behalf for one of my games. It gets a little attention but not much. X allows it, so long as it doesn't go against their rules, (no dm outreach, etc.)

comments.author: angry_cactus
comments.body: If you put enough work into your game to give it a cohesive playstyle, cohesive art style, and it looks like a polished finished game, then it doesn't really matter what techniques you used to develop it, as long as you are respecting licenses. Remember to promote your game to players, not just other devs.

replies.body: I'm not fighting, champ. I'm saying it could hurt your game if you disclose ai use because there are people who wouldn't even want to try your game once they see that disclosure.

replies.author: Mindestiny
replies.body:
Those people were never potential customers in the first place.  They're an irrelevant minority.  You don't set out to appease them in any way.

It's like worrying that someone won't buy your game because it has an anime aesthetic, or because you used the color blue, or there's a pig in your capsule.  You cannot please everyone, don't try.

replies.author: satupidfukignidot
replies.body:
They do, however, use the disclaimer as a call to arms.

Games which release with this disclosure are constantly review-bombed within their first few hours.

Also it's funny; we all know that AAA studios are embracing LLMs wholeheartedly, yet I've only seen a single AAA release since Opus 4.6 -- the first code assistant capable of replacing a senior engineer with a junior -- make this declaration; **High on Life 2**. It got review bombed all the same, but that developer had enough reputation (and capital) to overcome it.

Once again, antis claim to hate corporations yet their actions exclusively impact the little guys.

replies.author: NotaDevAI
replies.body: 'Remember to promote your game to players, not just other devs.' That's the core part I believe. Once you use AI and try to introduce to other devs(who are the most people on relevant communities), they just look at you with prejudice and hatred. As long as your game is built well, well designed, most actual user wouldn't care if you used AI or not.

comments.author: Destituted
comments.body:
Don't market to other game devs and Indie Game subs, they're mostly developers themselves.

I saw an AI game get posted in the World of Warcraft sub this morning and no one said anything about AI, they all were very interested in it.  The post is probably deleted by mods by now, but no one noticed or cared.

Other game devs and the whole Indie Game community are mostly out to kill AI game dev, but it doesn't matter.

I released a game a few years ago with very bad AI assets looking back on it, 10s of thousands of downloads and 100s of reviews, not one mention of AI from anyone.
